Explain how the sections are laid out

12-25 is the only section without citations; adult capabilities (assuming a "good" or "great" adult in each domain) are contrasted with 12-year-old capabilities; relying on the LLMs here (plural)

Justify covered behavioral domains

Mental rotation of objects is useful for simulations, e.g when imagining whether an object will fit through a door. May speak to a broader "mental transformation" ability 1

Cognitive mapping is useful for navigation but also manipulation tasks

Qualify contents

Many of the capabilities often emerge earlier or later in development; trying to present the averaged trajectory given all of the papers I compile for each stage and theories of cognitive development. For capabilities that often show up earlier (or usually show up earlier, based on recent findings), they often show up in a much more limited form rather than as the "full thing". A good example is scientific reasoning; it can be said that X-year-olds utilize a "control of variables" strategy, but only much older children are able to both reliably deploy it + use it to disambiguate systems that are relevant to the real world (e.g a cash register). A related example is in children’s sensitivity to evidence diversity during induction: children as young as five show sensitivity to evidence diversity in induction, but in a context- and domain-specific form (e.g they want diverse evidence for novel categories but not for familiar natural kinds) 2. Studies involving targeted practice/instruction show that children can learn behaviors much earlier than they would without such practice, but the degree to which the acquired behaviors materialize in lasting abilities (especially in a domain-general fashion) generally remains ambiguous.

There is often overlap between ideas expressed in each behavioral domain, especially "causal learning and simulation" and "executive functions"

Define each covered behavioral domain in depth

Aha! moments correspond to metacognitive prediction errors

Counterfactual reasoning

development of the counterfactual imagination

Essential for designing interventions; "If I wouldn’t have pressed button B, effect X would not have occured" -> test this

Inductive reasoning

-Three primary forms of induction: category-based induction, causal induction, and inductive processes in scientific thinking 5

Results in abstract, schematic knowledge, supporting feature attribution based on categorical generalizations, analogical reasoning, and causal reasoning 6

Highest correlation with general intelligence (inductive reasoning)

IR not only enables the online resolution of new problems but also the inducement of more general schemas promoting the transfer of resolution strategies between problems of the same class 6

five underlying processes: encoding (of the attributes characterizing elements), inference (of relations between elements), mapping of relations (seeking out a higher order general rule), application (of this rule from a new element to an hypothetical ideal completion), and response comparison (of this hypothetical completion with response options) 6
